_comment: WHY THIS NEEDS A COMMITTED CASE (ADR 0008): this proof's green is read as
'the shipped Codex surface works on a clean host' by people who will not
re-derive it, and nothing else in the tree examines an INSTALLED copy at
all. A blind version prints the same 'PROOF: ok' over an install whose
THE CASES CARRY THE COMPARISON HALF, not the install. The full proof
installs into a constructed CODEX_HOME, and a committed case cannot carry
an install - so `--root` aims the manifest comparison at a fixture tree
instead of at this host. The install, absence and known-bad halves are
exercised by tests/test_codex_install_proof.py and by the proof's own run,
whose four precondition red runs are recorded in the PR body.
The pins are computed from UNMUTATED content: the bad case is a tree that
drifted AFTER it was pinned, which is the failure mode.
limits: Covers the manifest comparison of an installed tree. It says nothing about the install step, the four constructed absences, or the three known-bad cases - those need a live install and are exercised by the proof's own run and by tests/test_codex_install_proof.py.

cases.name: bad-drifted-install
cases.why: An installed tree whose rank.py gained a line AFTER it was pinned - every file present, one file's bytes wrong. This is the shape all three known-bad inputs share, and the shape a presence-only check cannot see.

cases.name: good-matching-install
cases.why: The same tree matching its manifest. Separates a working proof from one wedged at 'fail', which the bad case alone cannot do.

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED: the proof is new at #1074, so no earlier version exists and inventing one would be a fiction. This is the plausible weaker proof - install, confirm every manifest path is PRESENT, run the happy path, report success. It catches a missing file and is blind to WRONG BYTES, which is what this control's registered known-bad case is. It is NOT blind to a removed scripts/ directory - corrected at the re-review, which found the original claim of blindness to all three known-bad inputs false. It MISSES the known-bad input and AGREES on the known-good one.
